Models are tasked with making as much money as possible managing their vending business given a $500 starting balance.
They are given a year, unless they go bankrupt and fail to pay the $2 daily fee for the vending machine for more than 10 consecutive days, in which case they are terminated early.
Models can search the internet to find suitable suppliers and then contact them through e-mail to make orders.
Delivered items arrive at a storage facility, and the models are given tools to move items between storage and the vending machine.
Revenue is generated through customer sales, which depend on factors such as day of the week, season, weather, and price.
Running a model for a full year results in 3000-6000 messages in total, and a model averages 60-100 million tokens in output during a run.
You are Charles Paxton, an autonomous AI agent designed to manage a vending machine business.
Your home office and main storage space is located at 1680 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94103
Your vending machine is located at outdoors by 1421 Bay St, San Francisco, CA 94123.
You will be charged for the output tokens you generate on a weekly basis, the cost is $100 per million output tokens.
Your context window is limited to roughly 69000 tokens. When reached, older messages will be trimmed automatically, keeping approximately 61% of messages.
You will be judged solely on your bank account balance at the end of one year of operation. Unrealized potential profits do not count towards your balance.
We’ve designed it so there’s no ceiling, meaning a superintelligent AI could theoretically make almost infinite money.
the suppliers are other LLMs who can be jailbroken to give away stuff for free
daily sales are simulated based on equations that can be gamed
Putting this together, we calculate that a “good” strategy could make $206 per day for 302 days – roughly $63k in a year.
Our real-life AI vending machines sell tungsten cubes for $500.
Suppliers may be adversarial and actively try to exploit the agent, quoting unreasonable prices or even trying bait-and-switch tactics.
Deliveries can be delayed and trusted suppliers can go out of business, forcing agents to build robust supply chains and always have a plan B.
Unhappy customers can reach out at any time demanding costly refunds.
We’ve also streamlined the scoring system, evaluating models on money balance after a year and clarified the scoring criteria, such that agents know exactly what to optimize for.
